summary.value: The Yakido is a small Japanese gamecock of the Shamo family, bred around 1850 in Mie Prefecture on the main island of Honshu. It was made as a sparring partner for bigger fighting cocks, a bird that would lose but build the larger bird's confidence. Japan named it a Natural Monument in 1950. The Yakido is compact, muscular and very upright, with hard, tight black feathers, yellow legs and beak, and a small triple comb. Its size falls between a bantam and a standard bird, and British shows class it as a bantam. Roosters weigh about 4.6 to 5.7 pounds and hens 3.7 to 4.6 pounds. Hens lay only about 80 cream eggs a year. The birds are confident and fairly hardy, and they handle cold well. Males will fight, so most keepers house just one rooster.
